goals.why: CQR dungeons are tiered by distance: the middle ring gives Age 3-4 loot. The Pirate Captain drops his revolver, the Necromancer cursed bones.
steps: Travel 1,500 to 4,000 blocks out (see the Ring Map page) and find a pirate ship or a tower.
Fight through the crew; CQR mobs use shields, potions and ranged attacks.
Defeat the captain on his ship or the necromancer at the top of his tower.

obtain.cqrepoured:captain_revolver: Dropped by the CQR Pirate Captain.

mobs.where: Commands a CQR pirate ship off the coast, 1,500 to 4,000 blocks from spawn.

goals.text: Defeat a Giant from Ancient Beasts
goals.hint: Giants (294 HP) walk the plains and ruins of the middle ring.
goals.why: A big damage check for Age 3 gear; it drops the Tough Glove.
steps: Look for a towering zombie in the middle ring.
Keep moving and hit its legs; bring food and a bow for when it gets close.

obtain.ancientbeasts:tough_glove: Dropped by the Ancient Beasts Giant.

mobs.where: A Giant (294 HP) that walks the plains and ruins 1,500 to 4,000 blocks from spawn.

goals.text: Craft an Iron Bow
goals.hint: Iron bows use iron; gold, diamond and elemental bows come later.
goals.why: A step up in damage over the stone bow, using plain iron.
steps: Craft the iron bow (recipe below).

goals.text: Block with an Asgard Shield
goals.hint: Iron and gilded shields use right-click to block and parry.
goals.why: Asgard shields follow on from the vanilla shield: sturdier, and Parry lets a well-timed block knock attackers back.
steps: Craft an iron shield (recipe below).
Hold right-click to block.

goals.text: Capture a structure with a Capsule
goals.hint: Capsules pack a build into an item and unpack it anywhere.
goals.why: Move a base or an outpost in one go; higher tiers need steel and vibrant alloy.
steps: Craft an iron capsule (recipe below).
Use it on the block you want to capture.

goals.text: Age 3 boss: defeat an Elder Guardian (or the Ferrous Wroughtnaut or the Skeleton King)
goals.hint: An Elder Guardian opens Age 4 (Nether & Power) for everyone on the server.
goals.why: Every age after Age 2 opens with a boss, never with a random find. When someone on the server defeats an Elder Guardian (or the Ferrous Wroughtnaut or the Skeleton King), Age 4 opens for every player at once: its guide chapter, the reward bag and the Bounty decree of the age you finished. Any one of them counts: an Elder Guardian, the Ferrous Wroughtnaut or the Skeleton King. Unlocks: Age 4 (Nether & Power): the Nether, Immersive Engineering steel, Ender IO, Actually Additions, Extra Utilities generators, Refined Storage, RFTools, Steve's Carts, Blood Magic, Industrial Foregoing and the first TaCZ guns.
goals.tip: Friends count: the killer, or anyone within 64 blocks when it dies, opens the age for the whole server. Nothing to craft or hand in. Type /sf3ages to see every gate.
steps: Where: Elder Guardian: inside an ocean monument. A cartographer villager sells an Ocean Explorer Map that leads to one.
Where: Ferrous Wroughtnaut: an underground hall closed with iron bars, found while caving.
Where: Skeleton King: Fish's Undead Rising crypts and desert tombs, 1,500 to 4,000 blocks from spawn.
Bring: A Tinkers or diamond weapon, good armor and food. Elder Guardian: milk buckets against Mining Fatigue, a Water Breathing potion. Wroughtnaut: hit it from behind after it swings.
Defeat it. Chat announces the new age and this goal ticks itself as soon as the age opens (ages open in order).
Drops: Elder Guardian: wet sponges. Wroughtnaut: its axe and helmet. Skeleton King: its crown.

goals.text: Optional: finish three Engineer bounties
goals.hint: Bounties are side jobs, never a gate. Use the Engineer Decree on a Bounty Board and hand in three jobs.
goals.why: Each player gets the Engineer Decree when Age 4 opens. A board with the decree offers jobs of Age 3 (items and kills from every strand) and pays one notch ahead, never a skip. Skip any job you do not like: the board offers new ones. Bounties count for this decree until the next decree arrives.
steps: Craft a Bounty Board (or use one in a village) and place it.
Right-click the board with the Engineer Decree.
Hand in three bounties; this goal counts them for you.
goals.tip: Lost your decree? Craft a copy: the decree and a paper (you keep the original). Old capstones still make their decree too.

goals.text: Travel to the Nether
goals.hint: Build a 4x5 obsidian frame and light it with flint and steel. Bring spare blocks and food.
goals.why: The Nether has blaze rods, quartz, glowstone, nether wart, wither skeletons and ancient debris. Many mods need its materials.
goals.tip: Beds explode in the Nether; use your Overworld bed for respawning.
steps: Collect ten obsidian and build the upright portal frame shown below.
Light its interior with Flint and Steel.
Bring blocks, food and fire resistance if available, and mark the portal on arrival.
Secure the return portal before exploring.

diagram.title: Nether portal
diagram.view: Side view (stand it upright)
diagram.note: The corners are optional. Light the empty middle with flint and steel.

obtain.minecraft:obsidian: Pour water onto still lava and mine it with a diamond pickaxe, or pour water into a Stone Barrel full of lava.

goals.text: Find a Nether Fortress and collect Blaze Rods
goals.hint: Fortresses are long dark-brick bridges. Blazes spawn near their spawners.
goals.why: Blaze rods make brewing stands, blaze powder, eyes of ender and many machines. Wither skeletons (for the Wither boss) live in fortresses too.
steps: Explore the Nether along one axis (east/west) to find dark red brick bridges.
Find a blaze spawner (a cage with fire) and fight blazes with a shield or bow.
Snowballs hurt blazes; fire resistance makes this much safer.

mobs.where: Blazes live in Nether Fortresses, around blaze spawners (a cage with a tiny spinning blaze inside). Bring fire resistance; snowballs hurt them. Carry a spawner home with a Diamond Chest Transporter for a blaze farm.

goals.text: Brew a Potion of Fire Resistance
goals.hint: Brewing stand, nether wart in water bottles, then magma cream.
goals.why: Fire resistance makes you immune to fire and lava: essential for the Nether, blaze farms and the Twilight Fire Swamp and Hydra.
steps: Craft a brewing stand (blaze rod + cobblestone) and fuel it with blaze powder.
Get nether wart from a fortress and brew it into water bottles (Awkward Potion).
Add magma cream (slime + blaze powder) for Fire Resistance. Redstone makes it last longer.

mobs.where: Blazes live in Nether Fortresses, around blaze spawners (a cage with a tiny spinning blaze inside). Bring fire resistance; snowballs hurt them. Carry a spawner home with a Diamond Chest Transporter for a blaze farm.

goals.text: Find a Bastion and trade with Piglins
goals.hint: Wear one gold armor piece and throw gold ingots to piglins to barter.
goals.why: Piglins trade ender pearls, obsidian, fire resistance potions, quartz and more for gold. Bastions hold netherite and gold loot.
steps: Wear at least one piece of gold armor so piglins stay calm.
Throw a gold ingot to a piglin (Q) and pick up what it gives back.

mobs.where: Piglins live in Crimson Forests and the Nether Wastes and guard Bastions. Wear at least one piece of gold armor so they stay calm, then throw them gold ingots to barter.

goals.text: Ride a Strider across a lava ocean
goals.hint: Saddle a Strider and steer it with warped fungus on a stick.
goals.why: A challenge: striders (saddle + warped fungus on a stick) carry you across lava safely.
goals.tip: Ordinary boats do not cross lava safely. Keep a marked return route.
steps: Bring a saddle, warped fungus on a stick, spare blocks and fire resistance.
Find a Strider beside a Nether lava sea, saddle it and mount it.
Hold warped fungus on a stick to steer across the lava, then dismount onto safe ground.

goals.text: Bring a Blaze Spawner home with a Diamond Chest Transporter
goals.hint: Only the diamond Chest Transporter can pick up a mob spawner (SF3 setting); the spawner keeps its mob.
goals.why: A blaze spawner at home is an endless blaze rod farm: rods are needed for brewing, eyes of ender and Create brass.
steps: Craft a Diamond Chest Transporter (recipe below).
Clear the blazes around a Nether fortress spawner, then right-click the spawner with the transporter.
Carry it home and place it in a dark, enclosed room with a kill spot.

goals.text: Grow Natura Nether trees and berries
goals.hint: Use soul-sand sieving recipes to obtain Nether saplings and berries.
goals.why: The pack disables natural Natura tree generation; its recipe and sieve routes keep these materials obtainable.
steps: Collect soul sand in the Nether.
Use JEI to select the soul-sand sieving recipe and mesh for the sapling or berry you want.
Plant the result on its required soil with enough clear space, then harvest and replant.

goals.text: Craft and power a generator of some kind
goals.hint: Simple Generators burn fuel, food or lava for power. They charge machines next to them.
goals.why: Most tech machines run on Forge Energy (FE/RF). A generator is the start of every tech path.
steps: Craft a Furnace Generator (recipe below) or any other generator.
Put coal or charcoal in it.
Place a machine next to it, or connect it with conduits or cables.

goals.text: Build an Extra Utilities generator
goals.hint: Fuel a Survival or Furnace Generator to produce FE for machines.
goals.why: Extra Utilities generators produce machine energy. Grid Power (GP), used by mills and some utility blocks, is a separate system.
steps: Craft a Survival or Furnace Generator.
Insert a fuel accepted by its recipes and connect an FE cable or adjacent compatible machine.
Confirm energy reaches the machine; GP mills do not replace this FE supply.

goals.text: Build an XU2 Magmatic Generator
goals.hint: Lava in, power out: the Magmatic Generator is built around a Furnace Generator.
goals.why: The second SF3 generator: lava from a crucible or a pump makes steady power.
steps: Craft it from gold, a lava bucket, redstone and an Extra Utilities Furnace Generator (recipe below).
Pipe or bucket lava in and connect a machine or cable.

goals.text: Move items with XU2 Transfer Nodes
goals.hint: A Transfer Node on a chest pulls items out and sends them along transfer pipes.
goals.why: Cheap SF3 item transport: one node per source, pipes to any inventory, and it works with upgrades for speed and stacks.
steps: Craft transfer pipes (smooth stone slabs, glass and redstone) and an Item Transfer Node (recipes below).
Place the node on the side of the source chest.
Run pipes to the destination inventory: items travel along them on their own.

goals.text: Build Solar Panels from Solar Flux
goals.hint: Panels make power in daylight; neighboring panels share it.
goals.why: Free power during the day with no fuel. Higher tiers produce much more, and neighboring panels share power.
steps: Craft solar panels (recipe below).
Place them under open sky, touching each other.
Connect one panel to a battery or machines with conduits or cables. A battery keeps power for the night.

goals.text: Store power in an RFTools Power Cell
goals.hint: Power cells store energy; every side starts switched off until you set it with a wrench.
goals.why: A battery stores generator overflow and keeps machines running at night or while generators refuel.
goals.tip: If a new cell stays empty, check its sides with a wrench first.
steps: Craft a power cell (recipe below) and place it between your generators and machines.
Every side starts disabled. Hit a side with a wrench (the RFTools Smart Wrench or another wrench) to cycle it: input, output, off.
Set the sides touching generators or cables to input and the sides feeding machines to output.
Stack cells on top of each other to share capacity.

goals.text: Make a basic Ender IO capacitor and a Machine Chassis
goals.hint: A basic capacitor is copper, redstone and gold nuggets; the Machine Chassis is iron bars and iron around a capacitor.
goals.why: Capacitors and chassis are core ingredients for the Ender IO machine path.
steps: Craft a Basic Capacitor (copper ingots, redstone and gold nuggets; recipe below).
Craft the Machine Chassis: iron bars and iron ingots around the capacitor.
Use the chassis in the Ender IO machine you want (the Alloy Smelter first) and give the machine power.

goals.text: Make alloys in an Alloy Smelter
goals.hint: Electrical steel and other Ender IO alloys come from the alloy smelter.
goals.why: Ender IO machines, capacitors and conduits all need its alloys (electrical steel, energetic alloy, conductive iron ...).
steps: Craft the alloy smelter (recipe below).
Power it and put ingredients in its three input slots (JEI shows every alloy).

goals.text: Automate turning Cobblestone into Gravel with a SAG Mill or Auto Hammer
goals.hint: The SAG Mill also doubles ore. The Auto Hammer works like a powered hammer.
goals.why: Crushing ore into two dusts doubles your metal, and gravel feeds the sieves.
steps: Craft a SAG Mill (or an Auto Hammer).
Power it and feed cobblestone or ores in; take the output with a hopper or conduit.

goals.text: Use Ender IO Conduits to power several machines at once
goals.hint: Conduits carry power, items and fluids in a single block.
goals.why: One conduit line can carry power, items, fluids and redstone together, keeping your workshop tidy.
steps: Craft energy conduits.
Run a line from a generator past your machines; it connects to each one.
Later add item and fluid conduits into the same blocks.

goals.text: Process an ore piece into ingots with an Actually Additions Crusher
goals.hint: Use an Actually Additions Crusher, then smelt its dust output.
goals.why: Ore doubling: each raw ore becomes two dusts, which smelt into two ingots.
goals.tip: Yields vary by recipe; do not assume every input always doubles.
steps: Craft the Crusher and connect FE.
Look up your exact ore or raw-material recipe in JEI and check its yield.
Feed the accepted input, collect the dust, and smelt it into ingots.

goals.text: Craft a TaCZ Attachment Workbench
goals.hint: Attachments are crafted at a bench built with Ender IO electrical steel.
goals.why: Scopes, grips and muzzles are an Age 4 upgrade: the bench needs electrical steel from the Ender IO alloy smelter.
steps: Alloy electrical steel (iron, silicon, redstone) in the alloy smelter.
Craft the workbench (recipe below).

goals.text: Convert blocks with an Atomic Reconstructor
goals.hint: Its laser converts the block in front of it; lenses change the effect.
goals.why: Makes Actually Additions crystals (needed for its machines) and converts many items with lenses.
steps: Craft and power the reconstructor.
Place a block in front of it or throw items into its beam path.
JEI lists every conversion.

goals.text: Make Steel with a Coke Oven and Blast Furnace
goals.hint: The coke oven makes coal coke; the blast furnace turns iron and coke into steel.
goals.why: Steel is used by Immersive Engineering and many other machines; coal coke is a strong fuel.
steps: Craft the Engineer's Hammer and read the Engineer's Manual.
Build a 3x3x3 cube of 27 Coke Bricks and hit the middle of a side with the hammer.
Burn coal into coal coke. Then build a 3x3x3 Blast Furnace (27 blast bricks) and smelt iron with coke into steel.

diagram.title: Coke Oven
diagram.view: A solid 3x3x3 cube of Coke Bricks; hit the middle of one side with the hammer.
diagram.note: The Blast Furnace is the same cube made of Blast Bricks.

goals.text: Craft a TaCZ Gun Smith Table
goals.hint: The gun smith table is built from IE steel ingots, logs and an iron block.
goals.why: Guns are a supply chain: the bench needs IE steel (pistols and SMGs), rifles, shotguns and snipers need Ender IO electrical steel, and heavy weapons need Twilight and Aether materials (Age 5). Ammo needs pressed copper plates and the ammo workbench.
steps: Make steel in the IE blast furnace.
Craft the table (recipe below).
Press copper plates in an IE Metal Press or a Create press for ammo.

goals.text: Build and power an Immersive Engineering Crusher
goals.hint: Follow the Engineer's Manual structure, form it with the hammer, and supply FE.
goals.why: The Crusher processes supported ores and other materials. Metal-equipment recycling belongs to the Arc Furnace.
steps: Open the Crusher entry in the Engineer's Manual and assemble its shown multiblock.
Use the Engineer's Hammer on the indicated trigger block to form it.
Connect FE to its energy input and provide output storage.
Feed an accepted item into the top and collect the result; keep yourself out of the machinery.

obtain.immersiveengineering:crusher: Not crafted: build the multiblock shown in the Engineer's Manual and hit it with the Engineer's Hammer.

goals.text: Make Brass using a Blaze-heated Mechanical Mixer
goals.hint: Catch a blaze in an empty blaze burner and place it under the basin.
goals.why: Brass unlocks Create's advanced parts: brass funnels, mechanical arms, precision mechanisms and trains.
steps: Craft an empty blaze burner and right-click a blaze with it (or capture one at a spawner).
Place it under your basin and feed it fuel.
Put a copper ingot, a zinc ingot and an IE electrum nugget in the basin under a running mixer: two brass ingots come out.

goals.text: Assemble a Simulated Contraption with a Physics Assembler
goals.hint: Glue a group of blocks, put a Physics Assembler on them and pull its lever: they become a moving physics object.
goals.why: Create Aeronautics builds real moving vehicles. The Physics Assembler turns blocks into a contraption with weight and momentum that you can stand on, and chests and machines on it keep working.
goals.tip: Every block has a mass. Turn on advanced tooltips with F3+H and each block shows its Sable Mass: wood is light, iron and stone are heavy. A slime ball merges two contraptions.
steps: Craft a Physics Assembler: a lever above brass casing, with andesite alloy on both sides (recipe below).
Build a small platform and place the assembler on top of it. It grabs the block under it.
Use Super Glue (or Honey Glue) on two corners to select every block that belongs to the contraption.
Hold right-click on the assembler and pull the lever. The blocks lift off the world and get physics.
To turn it back into normal blocks, use any Physics Assembler on the contraption again.

diagram.title: A first contraption
diagram.view: Layers from the bottom: a plank platform with the assembler on top
diagram.note: Glue the whole platform before you pull the lever. Pieces that are not connected split off as their own contraption.

goals.text: Lift off in a hot air balloon
goals.hint: A Hot Air Burner under a closed balloon of envelope blocks lifts a contraption into the air.
goals.why: Your first flying machine. A balloon carries you, your friends and cargo over mountains and oceans.
goals.tip: Hold W over the burner or an envelope to Ponder how balloons work. Right-click envelopes with dye to color them. Torches and glowstone on board light up the ground below while you fly.
steps: Craft a Hot Air Burner (IE steel plates, a block of coal, redstone and andesite alloy) and about 54 Hot Air Envelopes (wool and sticks).
Build a closed envelope, put the burner under it and light it.

diagram.title: Small hot air balloon
diagram.view: Layers from the bottom: deck, burner, posts and a 5x5 balloon
diagram.note: A bigger balloon lifts more. Lift gets weaker the higher you fly, so the balloon settles where lift equals weight.

goals.text: Drive a car on Offroad wheels
goals.hint: Wheel Mounts with Tires turn a contraption into a ground vehicle.
goals.why: Cars carry you and cargo across land much faster than walking, and later Rock Cutting Wheels on a Borehead Bearing turn them into tunnel-boring machines.
goals.tip: Hold W over a Wheel Mount to Ponder it. Heavy cars need more rotation; check stress with Engineer's Goggles.
steps: Craft Springs (iron sheets and an iron nugget), then four Wheel Mounts (andesite casing, a spring, an iron sheet).
Craft four Tires (dried kelp around a shaft) and right-click each one onto a mount.
Build a chassis with the four mounts, a seat and a rotation source such as a Portable Engine, then glue it and assemble it with a Physics Assembler.
Rotation into the mounts drives the wheels. A redstone signal into a mount from the side steers it; from the top it brakes.

goals.text: Craft a Mana Pool and a Mana Spreader
goals.hint: Generating flowers make mana; spreaders send it to pools.
goals.why: Mana powers all of Botania: infusing manasteel and mana diamonds, crafting runes, Terrasteel and the Gaia ritual.
steps: Make a generating flower (Endoflame burns fuel, Hydroangeas uses water).
Place a mana spreader near the flower; bind the flower to it with the Wand of the Forest.
Aim the spreader at a mana pool (bind spreader to pool with the wand).

diagram.title: First mana setup
diagram.view: Top view
diagram.note: Flowers within 6 blocks of the spreader. Feed Endoflames coal or logs by dropping them next to them.

obtain.botania:special_flower: A functional flower is made by putting its petals and a mystical flower into a Petal Apothecary (see the Lexica Botania for the petal colors).

goals.text: Infuse Manasteel in a Mana Pool
goals.hint: Drop an iron ingot into a Mana Pool with enough mana for the recipe.
goals.why: Manasteel makes Botania tools and armor; manasteel, mana diamonds and mana pearls are the three Terrasteel ingredients.
goals.tip: The pool does not need to be completely full. Each conversion consumes only its recipe cost.
steps: Generate mana with flowers and send it to a Mana Pool through a bound spreader.
Check the Manasteel recipe and make sure the pool has enough mana.
Drop an iron ingot into the pool and collect the converted ingot.

goals.text: Craft a Wand of the Forest
goals.hint: The wand binds flowers and spreaders and shows mana.
goals.why: Needed to link flowers, spreaders and pools and to activate many Botania blocks.
steps: Craft the Wand of the Forest.
Switch it to Bind Mode using its tooltip controls.
Sneak-right-click the Mana Spreader, then sneak-right-click the intended Mana Pool to bind them.
Use the wand on the spreader and pool to inspect their connection and mana.

goals.text: Craft and Place a Blood Altar
goals.hint: Stone, a furnace, gold and one Demonic Will make the altar; fill it with your blood using a Sacrificial Dagger.
goals.why: Blood Magic turns your health (Life Points) into powerful sigils, rituals and armor.
steps: Get one Demonic Will: throw a Soul Snare (string, iron and redstone) at a monster and kill it while it is snared.
Craft the Blood Altar (stone, a furnace, gold ingots and the will) and a Sacrificial Dagger.
Right-click the dagger while standing next to the altar to put blood in (it costs health; eat well).
Put items in the altar to transmute them with LP.

goals.text: Fill a Weak Blood Orb
goals.hint: Put a diamond in the filled altar to make a Weak Blood Orb, then right-click it to bind it.
goals.why: The orb stores your LP network. Sigils and rituals draw on it, and every altar tier needs a better orb.
steps: Fill the altar with at least 2000 LP.
Put a diamond in the altar: it becomes a Weak Blood Orb.
Right-click the orb to bind it to you, then leave it in the altar to fill.

goals.text: Make Blank Slates in the Blood Altar
goals.hint: Stone placed in a filled altar becomes a blank slate.
goals.why: Blank slates craft blood runes, and runes raise the altar to higher tiers for better orbs, sigils and armor.
steps: Put stone into the filled altar.
Keep it filled until the stone becomes a blank slate.
Craft blood runes from slates and stone.

diagram.title: Tier 2 altar
diagram.view: Eight runes one block below the altar, all around it.
diagram.note: The 8 runes go one level lower than the altar, all around it. Higher tiers need more runes and pillars (see the Blood Magic guide).

goals.text: Craft a Sigil in an Alchemy Array
goals.hint: Draw an alchemy array with Arcane Ashes, then add the base item and a slate: the Divination Sigil is redstone + blank slate.
goals.why: Sigils are reusable magic tools powered by your LP: the Divination Sigil shows your LP, others give water, lava, air jumps, an item magnet and more.
goals.tip: The Air Sigil needs a ghast-tear reagent made with 128 will and a Reinforced Slate, so it comes after the first Tartaric Gems.
steps: Build a Hellfire Forge and make Arcane Ashes in it (redstone, white dye, gunpowder and coal; no will needed).
Right-click the ground with the ashes to draw an alchemy circle.
Right-click the circle with redstone, then with a Blank Slate: it spins up and leaves a Divination Sigil.
Later sigils use a reagent from the Hellfire Forge and a better slate (JEI: Alchemy Array). Right-click a sigil to bind it to you.

goals.text: Collect Demonic Will in a Petty Tartaric Gem
goals.hint: Soul Snares make a monster drop Demonic Will; a Tartaric Gem in your inventory stores it.
goals.why: Demonic Will powers the Hellfire Forge and Will-based tools, armor and rituals.
goals.tip: Without a snare or a sentient weapon, monsters drop no will.
steps: Craft Soul Snares (string, iron and redstone), throw one at a monster and kill it while it is snared: it drops Demonic Will.
Put the will in the Hellfire Forge with redstone, gold, glass and lapis to make a Petty Tartaric Gem.
Forge a Sentient Sword (iron sword + the gem): every monster it kills drops will, and a gem in your inventory picks it up.
Use the stored will in later Hellfire Forge recipes (reagents, better gems).

goals.text: Build a CAD and cast a Psi spell
goals.hint: Craft Psidust (3 redstone and an ender pearl), then assemble a CAD in the CAD Assembler and program spells.
goals.why: Psi lets you program your own spells: mining lasers, flying, building platforms, healing.
steps: Craft Psidust: 3 redstone and an ender pearl make 3 (a pack recipe; later Psidust also comes from Psi spells).
Craft a CAD Assembler (iron and a piston) and the CAD parts: assembly, core (psidust in iron), socket and battery.
Assemble the CAD, write a spell in the Spell Programmer, put it on a spell bullet and load the bullet into the CAD.

goals.text: Make Menril Resin with a Squeezer
goals.hint: Menril trees grow in meadows; squeeze their logs for resin.
goals.why: Menril resin is the base material for Integrated Dynamics cables, readers and logic cards.
steps: Find menril trees (blue-tinted trees in meadows) and collect logs and saplings.
Place the squeezer, put menril logs in and jump on it.
Collect the resin into a tank or bucket.

goals.text: Build an Integrated Dynamics logic network
goals.hint: Cables, readers and variable cards made in the Logic Programmer.
goals.why: Read machines, inventories and blocks and act on them with logic, without any redstone.
steps: Connect Logic Cables and attach a reader to the block you want to inspect.
Open the reader, choose an aspect and encode it onto a Variable Card.
Place that card in a Display Panel on the same network to show the value.
Use a Logic Programmer for constants and expressions, and a Variable Store for referenced cards.

goals.text: Move items with Integrated Tunnels importers and exporters
goals.hint: Expose a source inventory with an Item Interface and configure an Item Exporter with a valid Variable Card.
goals.why: Move items and fluids along the same cables as your logic network, with filters and rates.
goals.tip: Blank Variable Cards do nothing. The Item Interface exposes inventory to the network; an importer/exporter needs a valid aspect card.
steps: Place an Item Interface against a source chest and connect it with Logic Cable.
Put an Item Exporter against the destination inventory on the same network.
Use a Logic Programmer to make a Boolean true Variable Card.
Insert it in the exporter's Export All Items aspect, then verify items arrive.
Use item predicates and filters before connecting valuable mixed storage.

goals.text: Craft the SF3 Workshop Table
goals.hint: Engineer's Workshop: install a furnace or crafting table in a module slot and add fuel.
goals.why: Engineer's Workshop runs several crafting and smelting modules in one table, all from one fuel slot.
steps: Craft the workshop table (recipe below) and place it.
Put fuel in its fuel slot.

goals.text: Add a crafting or furnace module to the Workshop
goals.hint: Each slot runs one machine.
goals.why: Each module slot works like its own machine, so one table smelts and crafts at once.
steps: Open the table.
Put a furnace or crafting table item into a module slot; the slot becomes that machine.

goals.text: Automate a Workshop recipe with an Auto Crafter upgrade
goals.hint: The Auto Crafter upgrade lets the workshop craft by itself.
goals.why: With the Auto Crafter upgrade the crafting module crafts on its own whenever ingredients are there.
steps: Craft the Auto Crafter upgrade.
Put it in an upgrade slot.
Set the recipe in a crafting module and feed ingredients.

goals.text: Expand the Workshop with a storage upgrade
goals.hint: Storage upgrades give the workshop more inventory.
goals.why: More room for inputs and outputs, so automation runs longer between emptying.
steps: Craft the storage upgrade and put it in an upgrade slot.

goals.text: Pack items into blocks with an AutoPackager
goals.hint: Turns 4 or 9 items into their block automatically.
goals.why: Compacts ingots, nuggets and gems into blocks automatically to save storage space.
steps: Craft the AutoPackager and connect FE.
Feed ingredients into its input with a hopper or item pipe; put output storage on its facing side.
Right-click with an empty hand to cycle the crafting mode.
Supply enough identical items for a valid 2 x 2 or 3 x 3 recipe, then check the output.

goals.text: Move items with a Hopper Duct
goals.hint: Ducts carry items like a hopper without sucking items from above.
goals.why: Cheap item transport: unlike a hopper, a duct does not suck items from the container above it.
goals.tip: Ducts transport items fed into them; a duct alone does not pull items from a chest.
steps: Place a hopper pulling from the source inventory.
Point its output into a connected duct route ending at the destination inventory.
Use the duct controls to check its direction, then send a few test items.

goals.text: Catch dropped items with a Funnel
goals.hint: Funnels collect items that fall into them.
goals.why: Collect drops from mob farms and breaking blocks straight into a chest.
steps: Craft a funnel.
Place it on top of a chest where items fall.

goals.text: Craft a Charset Pipe and Shifter
goals.hint: Shifters push items or fluids into pipes; pipes carry them to inventories.
goals.why: Simple, cheap item and fluid transport before you have power-hungry networks.
steps: Craft pipes and a shifter (recipes below).

goals.text: Power a Shifter and move items through connected pipes
goals.hint: Use a redstone signal to run a Shifter; a held redstone torch changes its mode.
goals.why: Your first automated item line: items move from one chest to another by themselves.
steps: Place a Shifter between the source inventory and a Charset Pipe, facing into the pipe.
Connect the pipe to destination storage.
Use a held redstone torch on the Shifter to cycle Auto, Extract and Shift modes; use a stick or Charset Wrench to rotate toward a connected pipe.
Apply a redstone signal and confirm items move from source to destination.

goals.text: Use a Shifter to transfer fluid through a Charset Pipe
goals.hint: Place a tank behind the shifter instead of a chest.
goals.why: Move water or lava between tanks without buckets.
steps: Put a tank behind the shifter instead of a chest.
End the pipe at another tank and power the shifter.

goals.text: Set and clear an item or fluid filter on a Shifter
goals.hint: Click a side with an item to filter; click with an empty hand to clear.
goals.why: Only move the items you want, so one pipe line can sort.
steps: Use a sample item on a non-output face of the Shifter to set a matching filter.
For fluids, use a filled bucket or compatible fluid container as the sample.
Right-click that face with an empty hand to clear its filter.
Check the Shifter status and run a small transfer to confirm the filter.

goals.text: Craft a Charset Tape Drive and Audio Cable
goals.hint: Tapes are made from ingots, reels and smooth stone slabs (JEI).
goals.why: Charset audio records and plays back note-block music.
steps: Craft a tape drive, a tape and audio cable (recipes below).

obtain.sf3extras:charset_audio_tape: Crafting table: three iron or gold ingots (or gems) on top, a Tape Reel left and right in the middle, three smooth stone slabs at the bottom. The reels must have tape on them.

goals.text: Record a short note-block melody onto a Charset Audio Tape
goals.hint: Connect note blocks to the drive with audio cable and choose record.
goals.why: Save your music to play again anywhere.
steps: Connect your note blocks to the drive with audio cable.
Insert a tape and press Record.
Play the melody on the note blocks, then press Stop.

obtain.sf3extras:charset_audio_tape: Crafting table: three iron or gold ingots (or gems) on top, a Tape Reel left and right in the middle, three smooth stone slabs at the bottom. The reels must have tape on them.

goals.text: Play your saved note-block recording
goals.hint: Right-click the drive with an empty hand and press Play.
goals.why: Hear what you recorded.
steps: Rewind the tape in the drive.
Right-click the drive with an empty hand and press Play.

goals.text: Place a SuperCircuitMaker component on a circuit board
goals.hint: Place components directly onto the Circuit board in the world.
goals.why: Build complex redstone circuits inside a single block, on a 7x7 board with four layers.
goals.tip: There is no component-picker GUI in this port; build on the board itself.
steps: Place a Circuit board with its top accessible.
Hold a component item and right-click the desired cell on the board.
Use an empty hand to inspect or activate the aimed component.
Use a Squeegee to remove a component and recover its item.

goals.text: Build a powered circuit that controls a lamp
goals.hint: Route a signal across the board to its edge.
goals.why: Your tiny circuit drives real redstone outside the board.
steps: Wire an input edge of the board to an output edge.
Power the input side; put a lamp next to the output side.

goals.text: Set a component's value or delay with the screwdriver
goals.hint: The screwdriver changes component settings.
goals.why: Timers, counters and repeaters need settings.
steps: Aim at a Constant, Timer or Delay on the board and right-click with the Screwdriver to increase its setting.
Sneak-right-click to decrease the setting.
Hold a stick in your offhand when you want to rotate one of those components instead.
Sneak-use the Screwdriver on an empty cell to change the editing layer.

goals.text: Record and place a paid circuit blueprint
goals.hint: Blueprints copy a design onto an empty board.
goals.why: Copy a working design to new boards instead of rebuilding it.
goals.tip: Copying consumes components. An incomplete bill of materials does not build a partial circuit.
steps: Use a Blueprint or Redprint on a completed Circuit board to record its design.
Carry all components needed for the copy and place an empty board.
Sneak-use the recorded design on the empty board to build it.
Check the copy with a Multimeter and a test signal.

goals.text: Create a Refined Storage system to store your things
goals.hint: Controller + cables + disk drive + storage disks make one searchable network.
goals.why: All your items in one searchable terminal. It also feeds autocrafting later.
steps: Craft a Solderer (quartz-enriched iron and sticky pistons) and power it: it makes the processors (printed processor, redstone, printed silicon).
Craft a Controller, cables, a Disk Drive, a Grid and storage disks (recipes below).
Power the controller and connect everything with cables.
Put disks in the drive and open the grid.

goals.text: Autocraft with a Refined Storage Crafter
goals.hint: Encode patterns in the Pattern Grid and put them in a Crafter.
goals.why: Ask for 64 of anything and the network crafts it from stored ingredients.
goals.tip: Ordinary crafting patterns are handled by the Crafter itself. Only processing patterns need an external machine.
steps: Connect a Crafter to the powered Refined Storage network.
Encode a crafting pattern in the Pattern Grid and insert it into the Crafter.
Put the required ingredients in network storage and request the result from a Crafting Grid.
For processing patterns, face the Crafter toward the external machine and return its outputs to the network.

goals.text: Move items with a Translocator
goals.hint: Place two Item Translocators in the same one-block gap between inventories.
goals.why: Very fast item transfer between two inventories that touch.
goals.tip: Basic transfer does not require a redstone signal; redstone control is an upgrade behavior.
steps: Leave one air block between the inventories and place an Item Translocator on each inward-facing surface.
Toggle the source attachment to eject and the destination attachment to insert using their center controls.
Send a small test stack and confirm the direction.
Add the relevant upgrades only if you need faster transfer, filtering or redstone control.

goals.text: Link an Ender Pouch to an Ender Chest
goals.hint: Chests and pouches with the same three-wool color code share one inventory.
goals.why: Reach the same inventory from anywhere in the world, even other dimensions.
goals.tip: Public matching frequencies share contents. Check the chest's ownership controls before storing valuables.
steps: Place an EnderStorage chest and set its three-part color code with dyes.
Sneak-right-click that chest with an Ender Pouch to copy its frequency.
Open the pouch and verify a test item appears in both inventories.

goals.text: Build a Quantum DSU
goals.hint: Stores billions of one item. Needs four Obsidian Chests and an Ender IO Machine Chassis.
goals.why: One block holds billions of a single item: perfect for cobblestone, dirt or ores from automation.
steps: Make four Obsidian Chests and an Ender IO Machine Chassis.
Craft the Quantum DSU (recipe below).
Pipe items into it from any side.

goals.text: Convert storage safely between a DSU and a Vast Storage Unit
goals.hint: Empty it first: a DSU alone in the center of a crafting grid makes a VSU and back.
goals.why: The VSU works with Simple Labels to show its contents on a label.
steps: Empty the DSU first: converting deletes the stored items.
Put it alone in the center of the crafting grid.

goals.text: Fill a Quantum DSU with a renewable resource
goals.hint: Pipe a renewable resource into a DSU until it is full.
goals.why: An optional long-term stockpiling challenge for a renewable-material factory.
goals.tip: This is a very large endgame quantity challenge, not a prerequisite for ordinary storage.
steps: Connect a renewable material source to a DSU with enough transport capacity.
Keep the source and storage loaded while playing.
Watch the stored count and add a safe overflow or shutoff plan.
Tick this stretch goal once the DSU reaches its capacity.

goals.text: Automate a Sieve with a Mechanical Sieve
goals.hint: The mechanical sieve sifts with power; send its output into storage.
goals.why: Sifting without clicking: a hopper feeds gravel in and the drops come out.
steps: Craft the mechanical sieve and power it.
Insert a mesh.
Feed gravel with a hopper and pull output into storage.

goals.text: Automate a resource with an Auto Heavy Sieve
goals.hint: Heavy sieves sift compressed blocks; the auto version runs on power.
goals.why: Heavy sieves sift compressed blocks: nine times the drops per sift.
steps: Craft and power the auto heavy sieve; insert a mesh.
Feed it compressed gravel (or sand, dust).

goals.text: Use an Auto Compressor to pack a renewable material into compressed blocks
goals.hint: It packs 9 items into one compressed block automatically.
goals.why: Packs nine items into one compressed block: feeds heavy sieves and saves storage.
steps: Craft and power the auto compressor.
Feed it cobblestone, gravel or sand from a generator line.

goals.text: Craft an Iron Seed
goals.hint: Iron ingots, intermedium essence and a tier 3 crafting seed in a crafting table make Iron Seeds.
goals.why: Iron as a crop: an endless iron farm that needs no mining.
steps: Upgrade essence: 4 inferium around an Infusion Crystal make prudentium, 4 prudentium make intermedium (the crystal is reused).
Craft a crafting seed and upgrade it to tier 3 with prudentium and then intermedium essence (JEI shows each step).
Craft Iron Seeds: 4 iron ingots and 4 intermedium essence around the tier 3 crafting seed.
Plant them on farmland; 8 harvested iron essence craft into iron ingots.

goals.text: Use Growth Crystals or Growth Accelerators to speed up crops
goals.hint: Place a growth crystal near crops, or growth accelerators under the farmland.
goals.why: Resource crops grow slowly; accelerators make them grow much faster.
steps: Craft growth accelerators (stone, inferium blocks and a diamond) or a growth crystal.
Stack accelerators under the farmland (more in a column = faster), or place the crystal near the crops.

goals.text: Craft a Soulium Dagger and collect mob chunks
goals.hint: Mobs drop mob chunks; a chunk with essence and a crafting seed makes a mob seed.
goals.why: Mob seeds grow bones, string, gunpowder, ender pearls and blaze rods without a mob farm.
steps: Craft the Soulium Dagger (soulium ingots on a mystical tool rod) and use it on mobs.
Collect mob chunks; smelting a chunk gives a blank tier mob chunk, and a blank chunk ringed with the mob's item (8 rotten flesh for a Zombie Chunk) crafts a chunk on purpose.
Craft the mob seed: the chunk and the matching essence around a crafting seed (JEI).

goals.text: Make Plastic for Industrial Foregoing machines
goals.hint: Latex from a Fluid Extractor on trees becomes dry rubber, then plastic.
goals.why: Plastic builds Industrial Foregoing machines (plant gatherer, mob crusher ...).
steps: Place a Tree Fluid Extractor facing a supported log to produce latex.
Pipe latex and water into a powered Latex Processing Unit.
Collect Tiny Dry Rubber and craft nine into Dry Rubber.
Smelt Dry Rubber into Plastic, then use it for Industrial Foregoing machines.

goals.text: Build an Industrial Foregoing Simple Machine Frame
goals.hint: The simple frame is dissolved from plastic, a pity frame, nether brick, gold gear and IE steel.
goals.why: Industrial Foregoing starts with IE steel: its frames now follow the SF3 tiers (steel, dark steel, draconium plus a Twilight trophy).
steps: Make steel in the IE blast furnace.
Craft a pity frame, plastic and latex, then dissolve a Simple Machine Frame in the Dissolution Chamber.

goals.text: Upgrade your mob farm to kill monsters automatically
goals.hint: Spikes or a Mob Masher saw kill mobs; an Absorption Hopper collects drops and XP.
goals.why: An automatic farm keeps giving drops and XP while you do other things.
steps: Place spikes or a saw at the kill spot.
Place an absorption hopper to collect drops and XP.

goals.text: Stop mob spawns around your base with a Mega Torch
goals.hint: Place a Mega Torch to suppress ordinary hostile spawning in its configured range.
goals.why: Reduces darkness-based hostile spawns around your builds.
goals.tip: It does not remove existing monsters or guarantee protection from spawners, raids or special modded spawning.
steps: Craft and place the Mega Torch near the area you want protected.
Check the mod's range display or settings and cover any gaps.
Keep entrances secure and handle any mobs already present.

goals.text: Assemble a Steve's Cart
goals.hint: Design modular carts in the Cart Assembler.
goals.why: Steve's Carts are modular minecarts that mine tunnels, build rails, farm and chop trees.
steps: Craft the Cart Assembler.
Put a hull, an engine and tool modules in.
Assemble the cart and put it on rails.

goals.text: Craft automatically with an RFTools Crafter
goals.hint: Crafters run crafting recipes with power.
goals.why: Crafts components by itself from ingredients fed in by pipes.
steps: Craft and power the crafter.
Set a recipe in its grid.
Feed ingredients in and pull results out.

goals.text: Show live information on an RFTools Screen
goals.hint: Screens display power, inventories and more.
goals.why: See your power, storage and machine status at a glance.
steps: Craft a screen and a screen controller and place them near each other.
Add modules (energy, inventory, clock) to the screen.

goals.text: Build RFTools Modular Storage
goals.hint: Storage modules hold items and can be searched with a Storage Scanner.
goals.why: Storage modules you can carry, plus a searchable interface.
steps: Craft the modular storage block and a storage module.
Insert the module and store items.

goals.text: Fly with a Simply Jetpack
goals.hint: The tier 1 jetpack is conductive iron, a basic capacitor, a leather strap and two thrusters.
goals.why: Your first flight: short hops and climbs on RF. Higher tiers fly longer and faster.
steps: Make conductive iron in the Ender IO alloy smelter and craft two tier 1 thrusters.
Craft the jetpack (recipe below) and charge it in an energy cell or charger.
Wear it and hold jump to fly; press the jetpack keys in Controls to toggle it or switch hover mode.

goals.text: Swap blocks with an Exchanger
goals.hint: An Exchanger replaces blocks with the block you choose, keeping your build in place.
goals.why: Change a wall from cobblestone to bricks in seconds, instead of breaking and placing every block.
steps: Craft an Exchanger Core (logs, red dye, ender pearl) and the wooden exchanger (logs, eyes of ender, core).
Sneak-right-click a block to select it as the new material.
Right-click blocks to swap them; higher tiers swap a bigger area.

goals.text: Quarry or copy an area with the RFTools Builder
goals.hint: Insert a shape card into the builder.
goals.why: Quarry huge areas or copy builds automatically.
steps: Craft the Builder and the correct card for your task: a quarry card for mining, or a shape card for building.
Configure the area using the card's selection controls and preview the bounds.
Connect FE and suitable inventory space for collected blocks or building materials.
Start with a small expendable area and verify the operation before selecting a large build.

goals.text: Program a ComputerCraft Computer
goals.hint: Computers run Lua programs; type "help" to start.
goals.why: CC: Tweaked follows OpenComputers: the computer needs an OpenComputers microchip (tier 1; tier 2 for the advanced computer).
steps: Place a Computer and right-click its terminal.
Enter edit startup.lua and write a small Lua program, such as print("Hello, Otto!").
Save and exit the editor, then run startup.lua.
Reboot the computer and verify the startup program runs.

goals.text: Program a Turtle to mine for you
goals.hint: Craft a turtle with a pickaxe, add fuel and run "excavate 8".
goals.why: A little robot that digs a whole quarry while you do other things.
steps: Place a Mining Turtle facing a small test area and put furnace fuel in its selected slot.
At its terminal, run refuel all and check that it has fuel.
Run excavate 3 for a small first quarry; leave space and storage for the mined blocks.
Scale up only after confirming fuel, inventory space and the return path.

goals.text: Build an OpenComputers computer
goals.hint: Assemble a computer with a CPU, memory and a hard drive.
goals.why: A full Linux computer in Minecraft for advanced automation.
goals.tip: The manual (right-click it) explains every part.
steps: Craft a Computer Case, a CPU, a memory stick, a graphics card, a screen and a keyboard (recipes below).
Craft the OC manual (book + microchip), then a Lua BIOS (EEPROM + manual) and an OpenOS floppy (floppy + manual).
Put the CPU, memory, graphics card and BIOS in the case; place the screen with the keyboard on it and a disk drive with the floppy.
Give the case power (RF from a cable or a Power Converter), press its power button and type install to copy OpenOS to a hard drive.

obtain.opencomputers:case1: OpenComputers parts use the mod's own recipes (circuit boards, microchips, iron); open JEI or the OpenComputers manual.
obtain.opencomputers:cpu1: OpenComputers parts use the mod's own recipes (circuit boards, microchips, iron); open JEI or the OpenComputers manual.
obtain.opencomputers:screen1: OpenComputers parts use the mod's own recipes; open JEI or the OpenComputers manual.
obtain.opencomputers:keyboard: OpenComputers parts use the mod's own recipes; open JEI or the OpenComputers manual.

goals.text: Program an RFTools Control processor
goals.hint: Visual programs that control machines and items.
goals.why: Program machines and item movement with a visual editor, no code needed.
steps: Craft a Processor, Programmer and Program Card, plus the CPU and memory hardware required by your program.
Supply the Processor with FE and install its supported hardware.
In the Programmer, create a small event-driven program and connect its operation flow, then save it to the Program Card.
Insert the card into the Processor, trigger the event and inspect its log or status output.
Add inventory access and machine-control operations after the simple program works.

goals.text: Infuse a machine to 100% with the Machine Infuser
goals.hint: Infused machines use less power.
goals.why: Infused RFTools machines use less power and work better.
steps: Craft the Machine Infuser and power it.
Put an RFTools machine and dimensional shards in.

goals.text: Wear Long Fall Boots
goals.hint: Long Fall Boots stop all fall damage.
goals.why: Long Fall Boots protect against ordinary fall damage while equipped.
goals.tip: They do not protect you from lava, the void or every modded damage source.
steps: Craft the boots and equip them in the feet slot.
Confirm they remain equipped before working at height.

goals.text: Store experience in an XP Ring
goals.hint: Carry an XP Ring to absorb nearby experience orbs; use it to release the stored XP.
goals.why: Store your XP safely and take it back when you need to enchant or repair.
goals.tip: The ring stores points from nearby orbs, not levels withdrawn from your current XP bar.
steps: Craft an XP Ring and keep it in your inventory.
Collect experience near it and inspect its Internal Experience tooltip.
Right-click while holding it to transfer all stored experience to your player.

goals.text: Upgrade to a Diamond Backpack with a Magnet Upgrade
goals.hint: Upgrade the backpack tier in a crafting grid; the magnet pulls items to you.
goals.why: Far more space, and dropped items fly to you.
steps: Upgrade the backpack tier by tier in the crafting grid (iron, gold, diamond).
Craft a magnet upgrade and put it in an upgrade slot.

goals.text: Shape blocks with Extra Bit Manipulation sculpting tools
goals.hint: Sculpting tools add or remove Chisels & Bits bits in spheres and cubes.
goals.why: Sculpt big curved shapes out of Chisels & Bits blocks quickly.
steps: Craft a sculpting tool (recipe below).
Use it on blocks to add or remove bits in spheres and cubes.

goals.text: Store Chisels & Bits bits in a Bit Drawer
goals.hint: Drawers & Bits stores bits by block type.
goals.why: Keeps your bit collection organized by block type.
steps: Craft the bit drawer.
Insert bits from your inventory.

goals.text: Pick up a mob with a Capturing Wand
goals.hint: Capture a mob in the wand and release it somewhere else.
goals.why: Move animals and mobs to your farms without leads.
steps: Craft the wand.
Right-click a mob to capture it.
Right-click a block to release it.

goals.text: Collect nearby drops with a Random Things Item Collector
goals.hint: Attach the basic Item Collector to storage to collect drops within three blocks.
goals.why: Gathers drops around farms automatically.
steps: Craft the Item Collector and attach it to a compatible inventory.
Place a dropped test item within three blocks and confirm it enters the inventory.
Keep enough destination space; use the Advanced Collector for adjustable range and filtering.

goals.text: Redirect a dropped item into connected storage
goals.hint: Item redirectors steer items moving across them.
goals.why: Steer item streams into the right chest.
goals.tip: The Redirector steers item entities; it is not an item pipe that inserts directly into a chest.
steps: Place an Item Redirector in the path of moving dropped items.
Use a stick on its output side to set the outgoing direction; sneak-use the stick to set the incoming side.
Feed a moving test item from that input direction and verify its new path.
Finish the path at a hopper or Item Collector attached to storage.

goals.text: Use the Voxel Projector to display an item
goals.hint: The projector shows a large hologram of an item.
goals.why: Big holograms for decoration and shops.
steps: Place the Voxel Projector and use an ordinary item on it to choose that item as the projection.
Use a stick for rotation, redstone for rotation speed, and quartz for scale.
Sneak while using those controls to decrease their values.
Use glowstone dust to toggle lighting, or an ender pearl to toggle randomization.

goals.text: Project a prepared VOX model with the Voxel Projector
goals.hint: Load a prepared .vox model through the projector's server command.
goals.why: Show your own 3D models as holograms.
goals.tip: This goal requires a prepared server-side file and command access. The ordinary item-projection goal needs neither.
steps: Have the server owner place the approved .vox file in config/randomthings/models/.
Stand at the projector and use /sf3voxel <model> with the file's model name.
Check the loaded projection, then adjust rotation, speed and scale with its item controls.

goals.text: Open a Chance Cube - if you dare
goals.hint: Breaking a chance cube does something random, good or very bad.
goals.why: A gamble: diamonds, mobs, explosions or something silly.
steps: Craft or find a chance cube.
Break it far away from your base.

goals.text: Assemble a Precision Mechanism with Create machinery
goals.hint: Repeat the JEI deployer sequence on a gold sheet; collect the finished mechanism.
goals.why: Precision mechanisms are needed for Create's advanced machines, arms and train parts.
goals.tip: This recipe is a deployer sequence. A press is used to make the starting gold sheet, not as a step in the sequence.
steps: Open Precision Mechanism in JEI and select Sequenced Assembly.
Feed a gold sheet through deployers applying a cogwheel, a large cogwheel and an IE electrum nugget in that order.
Repeat the sequence the number of times JEI specifies, using a loop or manual passes.
Collect the result and handle byproducts; assembly has a chance to produce a different item.

goals.text: Keep a useful Create production line supplied and collect its output automatically
goals.hint: Feed inputs with funnels and belts and send output to storage.
goals.why: A hands-off production line keeps making what you need.
steps: Supply inputs with funnels, chutes or mechanical arms.
Send outputs into storage.

goals.text: Fly a propeller airship you can steer
goals.hint: Propeller Bearings push a contraption; a Steering Wheel and Throttle Lever control it.
goals.why: Propeller bearings now need Ender IO electrical steel (Age 4) and smart propellers need vibrant alloy (Age 5).
goals.tip: Aviator's Goggles (leather and Engineer's Goggles) show thrust and stress. Gyroscopic Propeller Bearings stay level and suit helicopters. Thrust weakens high up; an Altitude Sensor reads air pressure.
steps: Start from a hot air balloon (or Levitite later) that can already hold its own weight.
Craft Propeller Bearings (wooden slab, Ender IO electrical steel, brass casing). Put sails or an Andesite Propeller on the front of each bearing: a propeller needs at least two sail blocks.
Give the bearings rotation, for example from a Portable Engine (it burns fuel like a furnace) on board.
Add a Steering Wheel and a Throttle Lever to control the rotation, then glue everything and assemble it.
Reverse thrust by reversing the rotation or with a wrench on the bearing.

goals.text: Run a renewable material through processing into storage without manual item transfers
goals.hint: Connect generator -> processing -> storage with pipes, ducts or a network.
goals.why: True automation: a material made, processed and stored without you.
steps: Choose a source (cobble generator), a processor (hammer, sieve) and storage.
Connect them with transport.

goals.text: Add an overflow plan so your resource factory can run safely
goals.hint: Send excess into a void (trash can, void upgrade) or stop the machine when storage is full.
goals.why: When storage is full a factory can stall or flood the ground with items.
goals.tip: Do not attach an unfiltered void to valuable mixed storage.
steps: Choose whether the system should stop when full or discard only a specific renewable excess.
Add filtered overflow storage and a void/trash destination at lower priority, or a storage-full signal that stops production.
Fill a test destination and verify the machine stops or routes only the intended excess.

goals.text: Drain a lake with a Ranged Pump
goals.hint: The pump removes fluid in a large area and stores it.
goals.why: Clears water for underwater builds, or collects lava as fuel.
goals.tip: Move the collected fluid out as the internal tank fills.
steps: Place the Ranged Pump above the fluid area you intend to clear.
Supply FE and connect an extraction pipe to an empty compatible tank.
Check the pump's configured range and let it drain; keep the work area loaded.

goals.text: Keep a remote factory running with a Chunk Loader
goals.hint: ChickenChunks loaders keep chunks loaded while you are away.
goals.why: Machines only run in loaded chunks; a loader keeps them running while you are away.
steps: Craft a chunk loader.
Place it at the factory.
Right-click it to set the radius.

goals.text: Link machines wirelessly with Flux Networks
goals.hint: Flux points and plugs send power anywhere on the same network.
goals.why: Send power across your whole base, or across dimensions, with no cables.
steps: Craft a flux controller, flux plugs and flux points.
Put plugs on generators and points on machines.
Open each one and put them all on the same network.

goals.text: Craft an Elementary Staff
goals.hint: Elementary staves cast fire, ice, wind and more from elemental essences.
goals.why: A magic strand for combat in Age 4.
steps: Craft the staff (recipe below).
Charge it with an essence and right-click.

goals.text: Craft a Soul Cage for Soul Shards
goals.hint: A diamond used on an obsidian, quartz and glowstone square makes a Soul Shard; kills fill it and a Soul Cage spawns that mob.
goals.why: Soul shards and Ender IO soul vials are one system: both feed the powered spawner.
steps: Build a flat 3x3 square: obsidian corners, quartz blocks on the edges and glowstone in the middle.
Right-click the glowstone with a diamond to make an unbound Soul Shard.
Kill mobs of one kind with the shard in your inventory: it binds and levels up.
Craft the Soul Cage (corrupted ingots and iron bars; corrupted ingots are vile dust from smelted soul sand, corrupted essence and iron) and put the shard in it.

goals.text: Find and fight a Lunkertooth
goals.hint: Deep Below is the Lunkertooth mod: an ambush fish that lives in ocean-floor ruins.
goals.why: Lunkertooth ruins hold a loot chest, and one chest in three hides a Lunkertooth egg. Its Esca, if it drops one, gives Greedy Eye (chest outlines) for the next ruins.
steps: Dive to the ocean floor ruins.
Open the chests carefully: one may hide an ambusher.

obtain.mimicfish:esca: Esca sometimes drops from the Lunkertooth; eat it for about a minute of Greedy Eye, which outlines nearby chests.

mobs.where: Lunkertooth lives in the ocean-floor ruins of the Deep Below mod (it is not a dimension): it hides in the ruin chests and ambushes divers.

goals.text: Open a portal to the Wyvern Lair
goals.hint: Craft Mo' Creatures' Wyvern Portal Staff and use it to reach the Wyvern Lair.
goals.why: A whole dimension of wyverns, ores and floating islands; wyvern eggs hatch into mounts that fly.
steps: Collect a heart of fire (fire ogres, fire manticores, Nether hell rats), of darkness (werewolves, dark manticores) and of the undead (frost or toxic manticores).
Bottle each heart into an essence, combine the three with glowstone into an Essence of Light.
Craft the Wyvern Portal Staff (eye of ender, Essence of Light, blaze rod) and right-click with it.
Bring blocks: the lair is islands over a void. Use the staff again to return.

goals.text: Defeat Barako, the Sun Chief
goals.hint: Barako rules a Barakoa village in the savanna; break through his masked guards.
goals.why: He drops the Sol Visage, a mask that calls down sun strikes.
steps: Find a savanna village of masked Barakoa (huts and a throne).
Defeat the guards, then Barako. Move when the ground glows: his sun strikes follow you.

obtain.mowziesmobs:barako_mask: Dropped by Barako, the Sun Chief.

mobs.where: The Sun Chief sits on his throne in a Barakoa village in the savanna, guarded by masked Barakoa.

goals.text: Defeat the Frostmaw
goals.hint: A huge ice ape sleeps in snowy biomes; its breath freezes you.
goals.why: It drops the Ice Crystal, which breathes frost on your enemies.
steps: Search snowy plains and ice spikes for a sleeping giant ape.
Bring a bow and good armor; keep out of its freezing breath cone.

mobs.where: Sleeps in snowy biomes (snowy plains, ice spikes). Its icy breath freezes you; fight it with fire resistance or from range.

goals.text: Defeat the Abyss Walker King
goals.hint: Abyss Walker castles stand in the middle ring, 1,500 to 4,000 blocks from spawn; the king waits at the top.
goals.why: A CQR tier 2 boss with Age 4 loot: the Walker sword and shield.
steps: Travel 1,500 to 4,000 blocks out (see the Ring Map page) and find a dark castle.
Clear its floors, then fight the king; it teleports, so stay in the open.

obtain.cqrepoured:sword_walker: Dropped by the Abyss Walker King.

mobs.where: Rules the Abyss Walker castles (CQR tier 2) in the middle ring, 1,500 to 4,000 blocks from spawn.

goals.text: Defeat the Vessel
goals.hint: The Vessel haunts ruined temples in the middle ring and summons copies of itself.
goals.why: It drops ectoplasm and its own vessel; a tricky fight against many copies.
steps: Explore ruined temples 1,500 to 4,000 blocks from spawn.
Find the real Vessel among its copies and focus it.

mobs.where: Haunts ruined temples in the middle ring, 1,500 to 4,000 blocks from spawn (84 HP), and summons copies of itself.

goals.text: Defeat the Harbinger
goals.hint: The Harbinger appears at night from 1,500 blocks out. It drops the Reaper Scythe.
goals.why: The Reaper Scythe and Necronomicon pages open Harken Scythe soul crafting: essence keepers and the soul tools.
steps: Travel 1,500 blocks or more from spawn at night, well armored.
Defeat the Harbinger and pick up the Reaper Scythe and pages.

mobs.where: Appears in the Overworld at night from the middle ring (1,500 blocks) outward. It carries the Reaper Scythe.

goals.text: Age 4 boss: defeat the Frostmaw (or Barako or the Abyss Walker King)
goals.hint: The Frostmaw opens Age 5 (New Worlds) for everyone on the server. The Twilight Forest and Aether portals open with it.
goals.why: Every age after Age 2 opens with a boss, never with a random find. When someone on the server defeats the Frostmaw (or Barako or the Abyss Walker King), Age 5 opens for every player at once: its guide chapter, the reward bag and the Bounty decree of the age you finished. Any one of them counts: the Frostmaw, Barako the Sun Chief or the Abyss Walker King. Unlocks: Age 5 (New Worlds) and the world gate: Twilight Forest and Aether portals work for everyone from now on. Also terrasteel, Extreme Reactors, Draconic Evolution, the End and the Wither.
goals.tip: Friends count: the killer, or anyone within 64 blocks when it dies, opens the age for the whole server. Nothing to craft or hand in. Type /sf3ages to see every gate.
steps: Where: Frostmaw: snowy biomes, asleep in the open; it wakes when you hit it.
Where: Barako the Sun Chief: the chief of a Barakoa village in a savanna.
Where: Abyss Walker King: the top of an Abyss Walker castle, 1,500 to 4,000 blocks from spawn.
Bring: Your best Age 4 gear: dark steel or Tinkers weapons, a bow or gun, healing and fire resistance. Fight Barako and the Frostmaw with ranged damage.
Defeat it. Chat announces the new age and this goal ticks itself as soon as the age opens (ages open in order).
Drops: Frostmaw: an Ice Crystal. Barako: his Sol Visage mask. Walker King: diamonds, emeralds and his sword and shield.

goals.text: Optional: finish three Nether bounties
goals.hint: Bounties are side jobs, never a gate. Use the Nether Decree on a Bounty Board and hand in three jobs.
goals.why: Each player gets the Nether Decree when Age 5 opens. A board with the decree offers jobs of Age 4 (items and kills from every strand) and pays one notch ahead, never a skip. Skip any job you do not like: the board offers new ones. Bounties count for this decree until the next decree arrives.
steps: Craft a Bounty Board (or use one in a village) and place it.
Right-click the board with the Nether Decree.
Hand in three bounties; this goal counts them for you.
goals.tip: Lost your decree? Craft a copy: the decree and a paper (you keep the original). Old capstones still make their decree too.

goals.text: Enter the Twilight Forest and secure a safe arrival point
goals.hint: Ring a 2x2 water pool with flowers and throw in a diamond to open the portal.
goals.why: The Twilight Forest is a whole dimension of bosses that unlock each other in order, with unique loot (Naga scales, Lich scepters, fiery tools).
goals.tip: Use the Magic Map (twilight) to find the boss structures; each boss unlocks the next area.
steps: Dig a 2 x 2 pool one block deep and fill it with water.
Surround the entire pool with a ring of dirt or grass and plants, including the corners.
Throw a diamond into the water and stand clear of the lightning.
Enter, secure the arrival point and mark the return portal on your map.

diagram.title: Twilight portal
diagram.view: A 2x2 pool ringed by grass, with a flower on every ring block.
diagram.note: Any flower or tall grass works, on grass or dirt. Corners can stay empty. Two water buckets fill the pool.

obtain.minecraft:poppy: Pick flowers in grassy biomes, or use bone meal on grass to grow some. Any flower or tall grass works.
obtain.minecraft:grass_block: Mine grass with a Silk Touch tool, or place dirt next to grass in the light and wait for it to spread.
obtain.minecraft:water_bucket: Right-click any water with an empty bucket. A 2x2 pool refills itself.

goals.text: Craft a Building Wand
goals.hint: Not Enough Wands: places a row or wall of blocks in one click.
goals.why: Extend walls and floors by many blocks in one click: big builds go fast.
steps: Craft the wand (recipe below).
Right-click the face of a wall: it adds a layer using blocks from your inventory. It costs a little XP.

goals.text: Collect Ironwood and Steeleaf in the Twilight Forest
goals.hint: Craft and smelt Raw Ironwood; find Steeleaf as Twilight dungeon loot.
goals.why: Twilight materials provide another equipment path and ingredients for the dimension's crafting recipes.
steps: Collect Liveroot and the other Raw Ironwood ingredients shown in JEI, then craft Raw Ironwood.
Smelt it into Ironwood Ingots.
Loot Twilight dungeon chests for Steeleaf; it is not harvested from a Steeleaf tree.

goals.text: Defeat the Naga and obtain its progression reward
goals.hint: The Naga lives in a mossy stone courtyard. Its scales open the Lich Tower.
goals.why: Defeating the Naga and collecting its scales advances Twilight progression toward the Lich.
goals.tip: Pick up the boss drops yourself so the advancement can trigger. Check the Twilight advancement tree if an area remains protected.
steps: Find the Naga Courtyard (mossy stone walls).
Fight in the open: dodge its charges, hit its head.
Collect the Naga scales and trophy.

mobs.where: Lives in the Naga Courtyard, a mossy stone-walled arena in the Twilight Forest. A Magic Map shows where.

goals.text: Defeat the Twilight Lich after completing Naga progression
goals.hint: Reflect the Lich's pearl projectiles to break its shields, then fight through its later phases.
goals.why: The Lich unlocks the Labyrinth, the Dark Forest and the Snowy Forest, and drops the Zombie/Lifedrain/Twilight scepters.
steps: Complete the Naga advancement and find a Lich Tower.
At the top, distinguish the real Lich from its invulnerable copies.
Hit incoming pearl projectiles back at the real Lich to break its shields; avoid the explosive fireballs.
Defeat its later phases and collect the scepter reward.

mobs.where: Waits at the top of the Lich Tower, a tall stone tower in the Twilight Forest. Defeat the Naga first or the tower stays sealed.

goals.text: Bring a trophy from a defeated Twilight Forest boss back to your base
goals.hint: Every Twilight boss drops a trophy.
goals.why: A memento of the fight and a decoration that animates when powered.
steps: Pick up the trophy the boss drops.
Place it at home (it plays the boss sound when powered by redstone).

mobs.where: Lives in the Naga Courtyard, a mossy stone-walled arena in the Twilight Forest. A Magic Map shows where.

goals.text: Defeat the Minoshroom in the Labyrinth and eat its Meef Stroganoff
goals.hint: The labyrinth is under the swamp and opens after the Lich. The Minoshroom drops Meef Stroganoff, which lifts the Fire Swamp curse.
goals.why: Without eating Meef Stroganoff the Fire Swamp burns you. It opens the way to the Hydra.
steps: Find the Labyrinth under the swamp.
Find the Minoshroom and defeat it.
Eat the Meef Stroganoff it drops.

obtain.twilightforest:meef_stroganoff: Dropped by the Minoshroom in the Labyrinth.

mobs.where: Guards the deepest room of the Labyrinth, under the Swamp biome. Opens after the Lich; a Maze Map helps you find the way.

goals.text: Enter the Aether and secure your return route
goals.hint: Build a glowstone portal frame and pour water inside.
goals.why: The Aether is a sky dimension with Zanite, Gravitite and three dungeon bosses that drop powerful accessories.
steps: Collect 10 glowstone blocks (Nether) and build the frame below.
Pour a water bucket inside the frame.
Step in. Do not fall off the islands: bring blocks.

diagram.title: Aether portal
diagram.view: Side view (stand it upright)
diagram.note: Corners optional. Pour water into the middle.

obtain.minecraft:glowstone: Glowstone hangs from Nether ceilings. Mining it drops dust; 4 dust make a block. Sifting dust also gives glowstone dust.

goals.text: Chop Skyroot and make Skyroot tools
goals.hint: Aether wood gives double drops with skyroot tools.
goals.why: Skyroot tools mine Holystone, the first Aether stone, and double drops of Aether logs.
steps: Chop skyroot trees on the islands.
Craft skyroot planks and skyroot tools (recipe below).
Use the skyroot pickaxe to mine Holystone for holystone tools.

goals.text: Read the Aether Book of Lore
goals.hint: The Book of Lore explains every Aether item you put in it.
goals.why: Explains every Aether item and block you put into it.
steps: Craft the Book of Lore.
Right-click it and put an item in the slot.

goals.text: Collect Zanite and improve your Aether equipment
goals.hint: Zanite tools get stronger as they wear down.
goals.why: Zanite is the Aether iron: tools that get stronger as they wear down, and needed for gravitite.
steps: Mine zanite ore (purple gems in holystone) with a holystone pickaxe.
Craft zanite tools.

goals.text: Craft an Aether Altar
goals.hint: The altar enchants items using ambrosium shards as fuel.
goals.why: The altar enchants gravitite and repairs Aether tools, fuelled by ambrosium shards.
steps: Craft the altar from holystone and zanite.
Fuel it with ambrosium shards and put an item in.

goals.text: Use the Altar to obtain Enchanted Gravitite
goals.hint: Enchant gravitite ore in the altar.
goals.why: Enchanted gravitite makes the strongest Aether tools and armor.
goals.tip: Gravitite ore blocks rise when disturbed; keep track of them while mining.
steps: Mine Gravitite Ore with a Zanite Pickaxe or better.
Put the ore in an Aether Altar fueled with Ambrosium Shards.
Collect Enchanted Gravitite and use it in the recipes below.

goals.text: Explore an Aether dungeon
goals.hint: Bronze dungeons are hidden inside Aether islands.
goals.why: Dungeons hold the bosses and keys to treasure chests.
steps: Find a bronze dungeon (holystone rooms inside big islands).

goals.text: Defeat the Slider in the Bronze Dungeon
goals.hint: Hit the Slider with a pickaxe; dodge its charges.
goals.why: Drops the bronze key for the treasure room (gloves, the Hammer of Notch).
steps: Use a pickaxe: swords barely hurt it.
Dodge its sliding charges and hit it when it stops.

mobs.where: Sits in the boss room of a Bronze Dungeon, hidden inside Aether islands. Only pickaxes hurt it.

goals.text: Defeat the Valkyrie Queen in a Silver Dungeon
goals.hint: Silver dungeons are large white temples on clouds.
goals.why: Drops the silver key: valkyrie lance, armor and more.
steps: Defeat 10 valkyries in the dungeon to earn medals.
Give the medals to the queen to start the fight.

mobs.where: Rules a Silver Dungeon, a white temple on the clouds. Defeat 10 Valkyries there to earn medals before she will fight.

goals.text: Defeat the Sun Spirit in a Gold Dungeon
goals.hint: Find the Gold Dungeon and return the Sun Spirit's ice projectiles.
goals.why: The final Aether boss; its treasure includes phoenix armor and the vampire blade.
steps: Prepare equipment, food and fire protection, then enter a Gold Dungeon.
Start the fight through the Sun Spirit's dialogue.
Dodge fire attacks and strike the ice projectiles back at the boss.
Defeat it and use the reward key on its treasure.

mobs.where: Rules a Gold Dungeon inside the largest floating islands of the Aether.

goals.text: Visit an Ancient City and escape the Warden
goals.hint: Ancient cities lie in the deep dark. Sneak and avoid sculk shriekers.
goals.why: Ancient cities hold enchanted books, echo shards (recovery compasses) and rare loot.
goals.tip: Sneaking helps but does not silence every action. Fighting the Warden is not required for this goal.
steps: Explore the Deep Dark for an Ancient City, bringing wool, food and a clear escape route.
Use wool paths and avoid activating sensors and shriekers; opening containers can make noise.
Loot carefully and retreat if warning levels rise or a Warden emerges.

obtain.minecraft:echo_shard: Echo shards are found only in Ancient City chests deep below the surface (sneak, the Warden hears you).

goals.text: Locate a Stronghold and travel to the End
goals.hint: Throw eyes of ender to find the stronghold, then fill the portal frame.
goals.why: The End holds the Ender Dragon, End cities, shulkers and elytra. Draconic Evolution starts here.
steps: Craft about 14 eyes of ender (ender pearl + blaze powder).
Throw one into the air and walk where it flies.
Dig down where it falls; find the portal room.
Fill the 12 frames with eyes and jump in.

diagram.title: End portal
diagram.view: Top view (already built in the stronghold)
diagram.note: Put an Eye of Ender in every frame that is missing one.

obtain.minecraft:end_portal_frame: Cannot be crafted or picked up: the frame is already built in the stronghold portal room. You only add Eyes of Ender.

goals.text: Kill the Ender Dragon
goals.hint: Destroy the end crystals on top of the pillars first.
goals.why: Unlocks the End gateways (End cities), the dragon egg and dragon breath.
steps: Bring a bow, many arrows, blocks, slow falling or water.
Shoot the end crystals on the pillars.
Hit the dragon when it perches.

obtain.minecraft:dragon_head: Found on ships in End Cities; a Dragon Head is not dropped by the dragon.

mobs.where: Lives on the main End island; reach it through the End portal in a stronghold. After the first fight, summon it again by placing 4 End Crystals around the exit portal.

goals.text: Collect Dragon's Breath
goals.hint: Use empty bottles on the dragon's purple breath cloud.
goals.why: Needed for lingering potions and some mod recipes.
steps: During the dragon fight, use empty bottles on the purple breath cloud.

obtain.minecraft:dragon_breath: Use empty glass bottles on the purple breath clouds of the Ender Dragon.

mobs.where: Lives on the main End island; reach it through the End portal in a stronghold. After the first fight, summon it again by placing 4 End Crystals around the exit portal.

goals.text: Resurrect the Ender Dragon with End Crystals
goals.hint: Place four end crystals on the edges of the exit portal.
goals.why: Fight it again for more experience; the egg only drops once.
steps: Craft 4 end crystals.
Place one on each side of the exit portal.

goals.text: Travel to an End City and obtain Elytra
goals.hint: End cities are on the outer End islands; elytra hang inside their ships.
goals.why: Elytra let you glide; with fireworks you fly fast across the world.
steps: Throw an ender pearl into a small End gateway portal.
Search the outer islands for End cities with a ship.
Take the elytra from the item frame in the ship.

obtain.minecraft:elytra: Hangs in an item frame inside the ships of End cities.

goals.text: Craft a Shulker Box
goals.hint: Two shulker shells around a chest. Shulker boxes keep their contents when broken.
goals.why: Portable chests that keep items when picked up.
steps: Kill shulkers in End cities for shells.
Craft a shulker box: two shells around a chest.
Break it with items inside: they stay inside.

goals.text: Eat an End Cake to visit the End
goals.hint: Each slice of the End Cake teleports you to the End.
goals.why: A quick trip to the End once you have been there.
steps: Craft the End Cake and place it.
Eat a slice to teleport to the End.

goals.text: Hatch a Dragon Egg and train it
goals.hint: Dragon Mounts: the biome an egg hatches in decides the dragon type. Tame and saddle it.
goals.why: Your own rideable dragon. The biome it hatches in decides its type.
steps: Place the egg in the biome you want.
Right-click it and wait for it to hatch.
Feed it fish to tame it; saddle it to ride.

mobs.where: Right-click a dragon egg (the vanilla one from the Ender Dragon, or a Dragon Mounts breed egg) to start hatching; keep it warm and wait for the dragon.

goals.text: Kill a Wither
goals.hint: Four soul sand in a T with three wither skeleton skulls on top. Fight it underground.
goals.why: The nether star is needed for a beacon, the Nether Star Generator and many endgame recipes.
steps: Kill wither skeletons in fortresses for 3 skulls.
Build the T of soul sand (deep underground or in the End).
Place the skulls last.
Fight with a strong sword, healing potions and milk (wither effect).

diagram.title: Summon the Wither
diagram.view: Side view
diagram.note: Soul soil works too. The last skull you place starts the fight.

obtain.minecraft:wither_skeleton_skull: Dropped (rarely) by wither skeletons in Nether fortresses. Looting helps.
obtain.minecraft:soul_sand: Found in Nether soul sand valleys and around fortresses. Soul soil works for the Wither too.

mobs.where: Never spawns on its own: you build it. Put 4 soul sand (or soul soil) in a T and place 3 wither skeleton skulls on top, the last skull starts the fight. Do it deep underground or in the End, away from your base.
